Rashi on Yevamot 15a:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג הכיר בה ולא הכיר בה איכא בינייהו - ול"ג אלא. לת"ק, דוקא דלא הכיר בה הוא דהוי מקח טעות, אבל הכיר בה — צרתה אסור'; ולאחרים, אפי' הכיר בה מותר', דקתני היתה ולא קתני נמצאת:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:10:1.english: This is how we read [the Gemara]: He knew about her or did not know about her is [the difference] between them - And we do not read "rather." According to the first tanna, it is specifically where he did not know about her that it is a mistaken transaction, but if he knew about her, her rival wife is forbidden. Whereas according to Acherim, even if he knew about her, [her rival wife] is permitted, since [the baraita] teaches "she was" and does not teach "she was found."

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:11:1.hebrew: כנס ולבסוף גירש איכא בינייהו - לת"ק, על ידי שגירש אחיו את בתו קודם מיתה, אע"פ שכבר כנס הנכרית והיו צרות זו על זו, מותרת — הואיל וגירש את הערוה לבסוף. ולאחרים, הואיל וכנס את הנכרית קודם גירושין דערוה, אסורה; אלא בתו של ר"ג אילונית היתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:11:1.english: [A case of one who] married and ultimately divorced is [the difference] between them - According to the Tanna Kamma, because his brother divorced his [Rabban Gamliel's] daughter before [his] death, even though he had already married the unrelated woman and they were rival wives to each other, she is permitted, since he ultimately divorced the forbidden relation. And according to the others, since he married the unrelated woman before the divorce of the forbidden relation, she is forbidden; rather, Rabban Gamliel's daughter was an aylonit.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:12:1.hebrew: יש תנאי בביאה - הכונס אשה על תנאי שאין עליה מומין או נדרים, ונמצא שיש עליה, לת"ק מהני תנאי והוי מקח טעות, ותנאי היה לו לאחיו של ר"ג בבתו ולא נתקיים, הילכך לאו אשתו היא וצרתה מותרת. ואחרים סברי דאין תנאי מועיל בביאה, דכיון דבעיל אחולי אחיל — כדאמרינן בכתובות בהמדיר (כתובות ד' עג.), אין אדם עושה בעילתו בעילת זנות — אלא משום דאילונית היתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:12:1.english: There is a condition in sexual relations - [If] one marries a woman on condition that she has no blemishes or vows [upon her], and it is found that she does have [them] upon her, according to the first Tanna, the condition is effective and it is a mistaken transaction; and Rabban Gamliel's brother had a condition regarding his [Rabban Gamliel's] daughter and it was not fulfilled, therefore she was not his wife and her rival wife is permitted. And "Others" hold that a condition is not effective in sexual relations, for once he engaged in sexual relations he waived [the condition] — as we say in Ketubot in [the chapter] Hamadir (Ketubot 73a), a person does not make his act of sexual relations an act of licentiousness — rather, [the rival wife was permitted only] because she [Rabban Gamliel's daughter] was an aylonit.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:13:1.hebrew: באחד בשבט - ושנה שניה הנכנסת לשלישית היתה, ונהג בה שני עישורין: מעשר שני כב"ה, דאמרי ט"ו בשבט ר"ה לאילנות, ואכתי שניה היא; ומעשר עני כב"ש, דאמרי בא' בשבט ר"ה לאילנות, ושלישית היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:13:1.english: On the first of Shevat - And it was the second year [of the Sabbatical cycle] entering the third, and he practiced two tithes with it: second tithe in accordance with Beit Hillel, who say [that] the fifteenth of Shevat is the New Year for trees, so it is still the second [year]; and poor man's tithe in accordance with Beit Shammai, who say [that] on the first of Shevat is the New Year for trees, so it is the third [year].

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:16:1.english: Ma'aziva - Clay plaster that is on the ceiling.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:16:2.hebrew: בשביל קטן - דסבירא לי' לשמאי, קטן הצריך לאמו חייב בסוכה:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:16:2.english: For the minor - For Shammai holds [that] a minor who needs his mother is obligated in [the mitzvah of] sukkah.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:17:1.hebrew: שוקת - אבן חלולה שתחת צנור המקלח מים מן ההר, והיתה נקראת שוקת יהוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:17:1.english: A water trough - A hollowed-out stone beneath a pipe that pours water from the mountain, and it was called Yehu's trough.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:17:2.hebrew: נעשים על גבה - מטבילים בתוכה, ואין בה מ' סאה, אבל מקוה שלם היה במים שבצדה, ומתערבין ממעיין השוקת דרך נקב כשפופרת הנוד:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:17:2.english: Were performed in it - They would immerse [utensils] inside it, and it did not contain forty se'ah, but there was a complete ritual bath in the water alongside it, and [the waters] would mingle from the spring of the trough through a hole [the size of] the spout of a wineskin.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:17:3.english: [He] widened the hole for it - They widened [it] and opened most of it to mingle [the water of] the ritual bath well.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:18:1.english: Joining of ritual baths - [This refers to] a deficient ritual bath that is alongside a complete ritual bath, and the water mixes through a crack or a hole. And the [required] measure of the hole to combine the ritual baths and render the deficient one valid [is]:

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:18:2.hebrew: כשפופרת הנוד - קנה שנותנים בפי הנוד, שיהא שיעור חלל החריץ כעוביה וחללה של שפופרת, דהיינו כשתי אצבעות:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:18:2.english: Like the tube of a wineskin - A reed that they place in the mouth of a wineskin; [meaning] that the measure of the hollow of the crevice must be like the thickness and the hollow of [that] tube, that is, about two fingers.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:18:3.hebrew: החוזרות למקומן - מתהפכות בחלל הנקב בריוח. והיינו כבית הלל, אבל לבית שמאי עד שתפחת רובה:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:18:3.english: That return to their place - [Meaning, two fingers] turning around freely in the cavity of the hole. And this is in accordance with Beit Hillel, whereas according to Beit Shammai [it is not connected] until the majority of [the partition] is breached.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:1:1.english: That they should perform ḥalitza - And [thereby] be married to outsiders in a permitted manner, according to all [opinions].

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:2:1.hebrew: מה נעשה לצרות הראשונות - שנתייבמו, ובניהם ממזרים אם נגמור הלכה שלא יתייבמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:2:1.english: What shall we do with the earlier rival wives - Who [already] entered into levirate marriage, and their children [will be] mamzerim if we finalize [the] halakha that they may not enter into levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:4:1.hebrew: לצרה עצמה - ואצרות דב"ה שנישאו לשוק קאי, והאי ומאי נעשה לאו אבנים קאי — דהא אפי' לב"ש כשרים לקהל — אלא אצרה עצמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:4:1.english: For the rival wife herself - And it refers to the rival wives [permitted] by Beit Hillel who married into the general public. And this [phrase] "and what shall we do" does not refer to the children — for even according to Beit Shammai they are fit [to enter] the congregation — rather, [it refers] to the rival wife herself.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:6:1.hebrew: רבי טרפון - מתלמידי ב"ש היה:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:6:1.english: Rabbi Tarfon - He was one of the disciples of Beit Shammai.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:6:2.english: When shall [my] daughter's rival wife come - from my brother into my hand [for levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:6:3.hebrew: ואשאנה - אייבם אותה כדברי ב"ש:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:6:3.english: And I will marry her - I will take her in levirate marriage, in accordance with the words of Beit Shammai.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:6:4.english: And I will marry her off - To the [general] public, in accordance with the words of Beit Hillel.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:7:1.hebrew: והא תאבני קאמר - ואם כב"ה, מה חידוש? כ"ע הכי נהגו:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:7:1.english: But he said: I yearn - And if [he meant] in accordance with Beit Hillel, what [is the] novelty? Everyone acts thus.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:7:2.hebrew: לאפוקי מדר' יוחנן בן נורי - דאמר תקנתא דחולצות:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:7:2.english: To exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri - Who stated [the] enactment that [the rival wives] perform chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:8:1.hebrew: מתלמידי ב"ש הוא - בתמיה, והלא מבני בניו של הלל הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:8:1.english: [Was] he among the disciples of Beit Shammai - [This is asked] in astonishment: was he not among the descendants of Hillel?

Rashi on Yevamot 15a:9:1.hebrew: אילונית היתה - ותנן: או שנמצאו אילונית, צרותיהן מותרות:
Rashi on Yevamot 15a:9:1.english: She was an aylonit - And we learned [in the Mishnah]: "Or [if] they were found [to be] an aylonit, their rival wives are permitted."

Tosafot on Yevamot 15a:13:1.hebrew: ונהג בו שני עשורין - בירושלמי מפרש דהפריש מעשר שני ופדאו, וחלק המעשר לעניים, והמעות אכל בירושלים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 15a:13:1.english: And he observed two tithes with it - In the Jerusalem [Talmud], it explains that he separated the second tithe and redeemed it, and distributed the tithe [itself] to the poor, and [with] the money he ate [food] in Jerusalem.

Tosafot on Yevamot 15a:15:1.hebrew: גמריה איסתפק ליה - הוה מצי למימר: וליטעמיך, היכי עביד כחומרי דמר וכחומרי דמר, והכתיב (קהלת ב׳:י״ד) "הכסיל בחשך הולך"? דהכי פריך עלה בפ"ק דעירובין (דף ז.) ובפ"ק דר"ה (דף יד:):
Tosafot on Yevamot 15a:15:1.english: He was uncertain as to his tradition - [The Gemara] could have said: "And according to your reasoning, how could he act in accordance with the stringencies of this [authority] and the stringencies of that [authority]? Is it not written (Ecclesiastes 2:14): 'The fool walks in darkness'?" For [the Gemara] asks thus against it in the first chapter of Eruvin (7a) and in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (14b).

Tosafot on Yevamot 15a:16:1.hebrew: וסיכך על גבי מטה ש"מ עשו - מכאן משמע דמ"ד לא עשו, אפי' היכא דב"ש לחומרא, היו עושים כב"ה לקולא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 15a:16:1.english: "And he placed [sukka] covering over the bed; conclude from here [that] they did act" - From here it is implied that [according to] the one who says they did not act [in accordance with their own opinions], even where Beit Shammai [rule] stringently, they would act in accordance with Beit Hillel's leniency:

Tosafot on Yevamot 15a:18:1.hebrew: עירוב מקואות כשפופרת הנוד כו' - וא"ת: והא תנן במס' טהרות (פ"ח מ"ט), ומייתי לה בריש פ"ב דגיטין (דף טז. ושם): "הנצוק והקטפרס ומשקה טופח אינן חיבור לא לטומאה ולא לטהרה, אבל טופח להטפיח חיבור"! ואמר ר"ת דנקב בעינן כשפופרת הנוד, אבל במים הבאים תוך הנקב סגי בטופח להטפיח. ואין נראה לר"י, דתנן במס' מקואות בפ' ששי (מ"ט): "כותל שבין ב' מקואות שנסדק לשתי — מצטרף, לערב — אין מצטרף עד שיהא במקום אחד כשפופרת הנוד. רבי יהודה אומר: חילוף הדברים. נפרצו זה לתוך זה על רום כקליפת השום על רוחבו כשפופרת הנוד" — משמע דלמעלה כשאין דבר מפסיק צריך שיהא צף על רומו כקליפת השום וברוחב שפופרת, ולא סגי בטופח להטפיח; ובנקובה זו לזו ומפסיק הכותל, משמע דצריך מים כשפופרת. ועוד, דאם אין במים הבאים דרך הנקב אלא טופח להטפיח, אין כאן נקב רוחב מים כשפופרת, שאין הנקב מרובע אלא עגול, כדקאמרינן "כשתי אצבעות חוזרות למקומן"; אלא ודאי נקב מלא בעינן, וכשצפין למעלה סגי בקליפת השום כרוחב שפופרת. ונראה לר"י דההיא דנצוק וקטפרס לא לענין חיבור מקואות איירי אלא לענין השקה — דאם יש כאן מים טמאים ומשיקן בנהר, ומחברן ע"י נצוק וקטפרס ומשקה טופח, אין חיבור, אבל בטופח להטפיח הוי חיבור; והשתא הוי "לטהרה" דומיא ד"לטומאה", ובהדיא מיתנייא לענין השקה במס' טהרות בסוף פרק שמיני. ובריש פרק שני דגיטין (דף טז. ושם) מסיק עלה: דלמא לענין מקואות ורבי יהודה היא — מכלל דעד השתא לא הוי מוקי לה לענין מקואות. והשתא נמי דמוקי לה לענין מקואות, מוקי לה דוקא כר' יהודה, אבל לרבנן לא הוי חיבור בטופח להטפיח; ולר' יהודה נמי טופח להטפיח לא הוי חיבור אלא משום "גוד אחית", כההיא ד"אם היו רגליו נוגעות במים" דאיירי בה רבי יהודה, אבל היכא דלא שייך "גוד אחית", כמו בקרקע שוה, לא הוי טופח להטפיח חיבור, אלא בעי מים צפים כקליפת השום. וכן משמע ד"נפרצו זה לתוך זה על רום כקליפת השום" אתי כרבי יהודה דהוזכר שם ברישא. ומה שקשה על זה בכל שאר הדיבור — פרשנו פרק שני דגיטין, ואין להאריך כאן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 15a:18:1.english: "A joining of ritual baths [is effective if the hole is] like the tube of a wineskin, etc." - And if you ask: But did we not learn in Tractate Taharot (8:9), and it is brought at the beginning of the second chapter of Gittin (16a and there): "A poured stream [nitzok], an inclined plane [katafres], and moisture that is [merely] wet [tofe'ach] are not a connection neither for impurity nor for purity, but [moisture that is] wet enough to wet [something else] [tofe'ach lehatpiach] is a connection"? And Rabbeinu Tam said that we require the hole [itself] to be like the tube of a wineskin, but regarding the water coming through the hole, [moisture that is] wet enough to wet [something else] suffices. And this does not appear [correct] to R"i [Rabbi Yitzchak], for we learned in Tractate Mikvaot in the sixth chapter (6:9): "A wall between two ritual baths that cracked vertically — [the cracks] combine [to form the required size]; horizontally — they do not combine until there is in one place [a hole] like the tube of a wineskin. Rabbi Yehudah says: The reverse is true. If they breached one into the other, [the water must be] to the height of a garlic peel over the width of the tube of a wineskin." This implies that above [the wall], when nothing separates [the two baths], it is necessary that [the water] float to the height of a garlic peel and the width of a tube, and [moisture] wet enough to wet [something else] does not suffice; and when one is perforated into the other and the wall separates [them], it implies that water [filling a hole] like the tube [of a wineskin] is needed. Furthermore, if the water passing through the hole is only [moisture] wet enough to wet [something else], there is no hole [with] a width of water like the tube [of a wineskin], for the hole is not square but round, as we say, "about two fingers that can return to their place"; rather, we certainly require a full hole [of water], and when [the waters] float above [the wall], [a height of] a garlic peel over the width of the tube suffices. And it appears to R"i that that [mishnah] of "a poured stream and an inclined plane" is not speaking about the connection of ritual baths, but rather about [purification by] contact [hashakah] — for if there is impure water here and one brings it into contact with a river, and connects them via a poured stream, an inclined plane, or [merely] wet moisture, it is not a connection, whereas with [moisture] wet enough to wet [something else] it is a connection; and now "for purity" is similar to "for impurity," and it is explicitly taught regarding contact in Tractate Taharot at the end of the eighth chapter. And at the beginning of the second chapter of Gittin (16a and there), [the Gemara] concludes regarding it: "Perhaps it is regarding ritual baths, and it is [the view of] Rabbi Yehudah" — which implies that until now [the Gemara] had not established it as referring to ritual baths. And even now that it establishes it as referring to ritual baths, it establishes it specifically according to Rabbi Yehudah, whereas according to the Rabbis it is not a connection with [moisture] wet enough to wet [something else]. And even according to Rabbi Yehudah, [moisture] wet enough to wet [something else] is a connection only because of [the principle of] "extend and bring down" [gud achit], like that case of "if his feet were touching the water" which Rabbi Yehudah is discussing; however, where "extend and bring down" does not apply, such as on level ground, [moisture] wet enough to wet [something else] is not a connection, rather it requires water floating [to the height of] a garlic peel. And so it is implied that "if they breached one into the other, [to] the height of a garlic peel" follows Rabbi Yehudah, who was mentioned there in the first clause. And as for the difficulties raised against this throughout the rest of that passage — we have explained [them] in the second chapter of Gittin, and there is no need to elaborate here.
